t: The first sentence of section 22(i) of the Second Liberty Bond Act, as amended (31 U.S.C. 757c(i)), is amended by inserting “and savings notes” after “bonds”, The second sentence of such section is is amended by striking out “such bonds,” and inserting in lieu thereof “such bonds and notes,”.

fable.w: This section is a purely technical amendment that adds "savings notes" alongside bonds in the Second Liberty Bond Act. It involves no consultation, hearing, rulemaking, advisory body, or right to sue involving any party outside the federal government, so there is no tempting participation reading to credit.
fable.s: is amended by inserting “and savings notes” after “bonds”

opus.w: This is a purely technical amendment that extends an existing provision to cover savings notes as well as bonds. Nothing in the text requires or allows rulemaking, a comment period, a hearing, consultation with outside parties, or a right to sue. Reading in participation would mean guessing at what the amended provision says, which this text does not show.
opus.s: is amended by inserting “and savings notes” after “bonds”
opus.b:
1. **Thinking it through:** The tempting reading is that because the amended provision (section 22(i) of the Second Liberty Bond Act) may involve Treasury authority over savings bonds, possibly including rules, this counts as rulemaking. That fails because the section itself only adds "savings notes" next to "bonds" and changes "such bonds" to "such bonds and notes." It does not mention any regulation, consultation, hearing, advisory body or right to sue, and it involves no one outside the federal government.

qwen_chat.w: This section is a technical amendment to the Second Liberty Bond Act, expanding the definition of covered instruments to include savings notes. It does not establish any process for public comment, consultation with outside entities, or advisory committees. The text merely changes statutory definitions and does not involve any interaction with parties outside the federal government in the decision-making process.
qwen_chat.s: The first sentence of section 22(i) of the Second Liberty Bond Act, as amended (31 U.S.C. 757c(i)), is amended by inserting “and savings notes” after “bonds”, The second sentence of such section is is amended by striking out “such bonds,” and inserting in lieu thereof “such bonds and notes,”.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that amending the definition of "bonds" to include "savings notes" implicitly changes who can participate in purchasing them, but the text itself contains no procedural mechanism for public input, consultation, or advisory involvement. It is purely a definitional and textual amendment to existing statutory language regarding financial instruments.
